meanings.note: Masculine: acteur. Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor'). Standard feminine noun meaning 'actress'.

examples.text: Je ne suis pas actrice. Je veux juste voir Mathias.
examples.trans: I'm not an actress. I just want to see Mathias.

meanings.note: For actors, sport stars, writers. Masculine noun ('le agent', plural 'les agents') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'agent'.

examples.trans: Do I still have an agent?

examples.text: Arlette, c'est la doyenne des agents à Paris.
examples.trans: Arlette is the most senior agent in Paris.

meanings.note: Feminine form of agent. Feminine noun ('la agente', plural 'les agentes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'agent'.

examples.trans: She would make an excellent agent.

examples.text: Prenez soin de vous... Ma Nouvelle Agente.
examples.trans: Take care of yourself... My New Agent.

meanings.note: With things and places. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to like'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'aimé').
With people. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to like'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'aimé').

examples.text: Tu n'aimais pas Mandelieu? C'est un bel endroit.
examples.trans: Didn't you like Mandelieu? It's a lovely place.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'fun'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: C'est amusant pour des enfants de dix ans.

meanings.note: invariable in the plural; cet après-midi = this afternoon

examples.text: Tout le monde en place pour cet après-midi.

examples.text: Je veux réussir ma scène cet après-midi.
examples.trans: I want to succeed in my scene this afternoon.

meanings.note: Arrête! / arrêtez!. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to stop'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'arrêté').
Arrête! / arrêtez!. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to stop'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'arrêté').

examples.text: Il arrête de travailler à six heures.
Sans toi, je crois que j'arrêterais ce métier.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Attendez-moi deux minutes devant le bureau!

examples.text: Nous attendons un appel très important de Los Angeles.
examples.trans: We are waiting for a very important call from Los Angeles.

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'today'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: J'ai essayé de t'appeler. C'est non-stop au boulot aujourd'hui.
